notes: Multi-country file: IE (EUR) and NZ (NZD); each vendor carries its own country. IE: two food-truck tools with a price: Order Tiger (EUR 59 is the page's 'plans from' figure; the plan cards render in USD by default behind a JS currency switch, and Ireland is never named, only an EU/EUR region) and Click & Collection (EUR 29 + 2.9%; upgraded to focus food_truck from its own blog 'We are dedicated to supporting the food trucks of Ireland!'; Irish governing law). Flipdish is restaurant/takeaway only (nearest_local, kept for reference); its online-ordering page shows three untitled EUR price cards (69/79/99 billed monthly), so the stored 'Website & Mobile App' plan name could not be confirmed. GloriaFood marked not_relevant: its own site says 'GloriaFood will reach end of life on April 30, 2027.' and it is USD-only with no Ireland presence. Zur (new, IE app) unreadable: zur.ie and www.zur.ie return 404; likely a marketplace anyway. Square Online IE came up in a search but was not researched (IE already had 2 food-truck tools). NZ: HungryTrucks still shows the promo 'Normally $46, now $0.99/mo for 6 months!' with NO currency stated (NZD assumed). Bopple's currency switch defaults to AUD; the page's own script prices NZ the same as AU ($49; US is $29), and its fee page gives NZ '2.4% + $0.10' per order from 1 October 2026. MOBI is quote-only (price null). Street Food Spot shows only 'Free to list.' (price null). SmakSpace (stored candidate, first check) qualifies: names food trucks, order-ahead app, NZ$49/mo Starter, not GST registered. HungryTrucks and Street Food Spot are shared consumer apps across many trucks rather than each truck's own ordering site. Several price quotes come from run-together rendered text (Bopple '$49per month', SmakSpace 'NZ$49≈ NZ$39 /mo', GloriaFood 'US$ 29 per month' with markup stripped) and may need loosening in the quote checker. No extra NZ search was needed (HungryTrucks and SmakSpace both qualify with a price). Bopple NZ price was read from bopple.com's own pricing page HTML and its JS bundle (downloaded with curl, one request at a time). Because both IE and NZ now have 2 food-truck tools with a price, Flipdish (IE) and Bopple (NZ) are nearest_local fallbacks under the 24 Nov rule; they are kept as verdict eligible with full answers so the reviewer can decide whether to show them.
